early.title: Vote early, October 24 to November 1
early.body: Nine days, every day, including the weekend. Early voting works exactly like Election Day, same ballot, same machines, and the lines are short. Your early voting site is chosen by your city or township clerk and is often not the same building as your Election Day polling place, so look it up rather than assuming.

dates.what: Last day to register online. After this you register in person at your clerk, right through Election Day.
Early voting opens. Nine days, every day, at your early voting site.
Election Day. Polls open 7 am to 8 pm. Not registered yet? Your clerk's office registers you and hands you a ballot until 8 pm.

mi.title: Vote at school or vote at home. Your call.
mi.body: You can be registered at one address, and Michigan lets a student pick either one. Registered here means you vote on campus, in the races that decide things where you actually live, and this page will walk you to the door. Registered at home means voting there. Pick the one you will actually do.
mi.tip: Registering at your campus address moves the address on your Michigan license or state ID at the same time. That is how the state works, not something you did wrong.

other.title: You can register here, at your campus address.
other.body: Going to school in Michigan is enough to register in Michigan, and your campus address is the one to use. One thing to know before you do: you can only be registered in one state, so registering here cancels your registration back home.
other.tip: Your license from home is still your photo ID at the polls. You do not need a Michigan one.

register.online: Online takes a few minutes and works until October 19. You will need a Michigan license or state ID, or the last four digits of your Social Security number.
register.person: Anyone can register in person at their city or township clerk, and that works right up to 8 pm on Election Day. Bring one thing that shows your name and your campus address.
register.noSsn: No Social Security number and no Michigan ID? Register in person. The clerk can take a signed statement instead.

proof.intro: Registering in person? Bring one of these with your name and campus address on it. A screen on your phone counts.
items: Your student portal, on your phone, showing your name and on campus address
Financial aid paperwork or your enrollment forms
A utility bill, bank statement, or insurance document
A paycheck or a check from a government agency
A Michigan license or state ID, or a US passport

id.intro: At the polls you will be asked for photo ID. Your student ID is one.
items: Student ID with your photo from your school
Michigan driver's license or state ID
A driver's license or ID from any other state
US passport, military ID, tribal ID, or any government photo ID
id.none: Forgot it? You still vote. You sign a short statement that you did not have ID on you and your ballot counts like anyone else's.

eligible: Living at the address you register at for 30 days by Election Day
Not currently serving a sentence in jail or prison
